title: Working from Home: Freedom or Trap?
text:
When the pandemic started, millions of office workers suddenly had to work from home. At first, many people were excited. They no longer had to sit in traffic for an hour every morning, and they could finally spend more time with their families.

However, after a few months, some problems came up. Many employees found it hard to separate their work life from their private life. Because their laptop was always on the kitchen table, they kept checking emails late at night. Others felt lonely, as they missed the small conversations with colleagues that used to happen around the coffee machine.

Companies also had to figure out new ways of working. Managers who were used to seeing their team every day had to learn to trust people they could not see. Some companies decided to put off important decisions about offices until the situation was clearer.

Today, most experts agree that the best solution is a mix of both. Working from home two or three days a week gives people flexibility, while days in the office help teams stay connected. As a result, many companies now offer hybrid contracts, and employees who are used to this model rarely want to go back.

ex: Sorry, something came up and I can't come tonight.
Try to separate your work from your free time.
I used to walk to work, but now I drive.
I can't figure out how this printer works.
She is used to getting up early.
You can trust him with the keys.
Don't put off your homework until Sunday.
It rained all day. As a result, the match was cancelled.

questions.q: Why were many workers happy at the beginning?
options: They didn't have to travel to the office.
questions.explain_tr: Metin: "They no longer had to sit in traffic…" → işe gidip gelmek zorunda değillerdi.

questions.q: What problem is NOT mentioned in the text?
questions.explain_tr: İnternet yavaşlığından hiç bahsedilmiyor; diğer üçü metinde var.

questions.q: What can we infer about managers?
options: They preferred to control their teams by seeing them.
They wanted everyone to work from home forever.
questions.explain_tr: "were used to seeing their team every day" ve "had to learn to trust" → ekibi görerek kontrol etmeye alışkındılar.

questions.q: In the text, "put off important decisions" means…
questions.explain_tr: **put off** = ertelemek. İptal etmek **call off** olurdu.
